chain: The law expands adult eligibility.
Eligible low-income adults can obtain public insurance.
Coverage lowers the number recorded uninsured.
The terminal is legal eligibility plus a recorded enrollment; income, age, residency and service availability must be read, not assumed.
whyAnswers.reverseOnRepeal: Remove or replace the current legal exposure prospectively; enrollment, services, contracts and accumulated outcomes need their own records, not an immediate numerical inverse.
whyAnswers.who: The ACA raised coverage 5.9 points in expansion states and 3.0 in others: about 2.9 points among adults 19 to 64 from expansion, about 1.8 points across all ages, about -15% of a non-expansion state's 2024 uninsured rate.
whyAnswers.placeVariation: Preserve the existing per-world/per-place draw and recorded range where present. Statutory reach, actual eligible people and service capacity differ; no blanket state coverage is inferred.
whyAnswers.source: Courtemanche, Marton, Ukert, Yelowitz and Zapata 2017 (JPAM)

chain: The law adds work or exemption conditions to coverage.
A recipient must satisfy and document those conditions.
Recorded failure or administrative loss can end coverage.

chain: Assistance eligibility adds work or training conditions.
Recipients outside exemptions must satisfy the rule.
A refusal or coverage exit reduces recorded participation.
The terminal is an actual benefit eligibility/refusal record; a population reduction is not an automatic deduction from every household.
whyAnswers.reverseOnRepeal: Remove or replace the current legal exposure prospectively; enrollment, services, contracts and accumulated outcomes need their own records, not an immediate numerical inverse.
whyAnswers.who: Work requirements cut participation 53% among adults subject to them, with no gain in employment; adults 18 to 49 without a disability in childless households, those the requirement reaches, are 9.8% of SNAP participants, so about 5.2% fewer residents receive SNAP. The range runs from the 64% exit rate among incumbents to half the effect, for states where many of those adults are already exempt or covered by a waiver.

chain: A crisis-response service can dispatch health responders to some low-level calls.
Their treatment and diversion can replace arrest or offense recording in those calls.

The terminal is actual responder dispatch and case handling; this existing violent-crime proxy requires correction/research rather than being called proven.

chain: Reversal distribution can put naloxone within reach during an opioid overdose.

whyAnswers.who: Naloxone access laws: opioid deaths 9 to 11% lower in one study, no net drop in another; opioids are most, not all, overdose deaths

chain: The law grants qualifying consumers access, correction and deletion rights.
Covered businesses face compliance and enforcement obligations.
Only part of the business and worker population falls within the statutes.
The terminal is a legal right and covered-business duty; the about-zero median-earnings slot is not proof that no business pays compliance costs.

whyAnswers.who: State privacy laws bind only large data holders: the common model reaches a business handling data on 100,000 of the state's consumers, and California's also one with $25 million in revenue. The cost falls on data firms and app makers, which lost investment and apps under Europe's rule, too small a share of a state's workers to move its median earnings

chain: An operative platform rule requires an age check.
A platform may refuse access when verification fails.
A refusal is different from a measured change in school completion.
The terminal is a legal rule and access decision; injunctions and absent outcome evidence prevent inferring a graduation gain.
whyAnswers.reverseOnRepeal: No unsupported opposite outcome is inferred.
whyAnswers.who: Courts blocked most state laws requiring platforms to check ages before they took effect (Arkansas, Ohio, Utah, California, Texas, Maryland), and no study has measured an effect on students. Facebook's arrival at colleges hurt students' mental health and schoolwork, but an age check on a platform teenagers already use is not the reverse of its arrival
